subject: Proposal: convert monthly plan to annual reserved commitment with tranche credits
messages:
From: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@nimblehealth.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question and next steps

Hey Logan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our CFO asked whether we can move from month-to-month billing to an annual prepaid commitment to reduce unit cost. High level questions: what magnitude of discount do we get for a 12‑month commit that starts 1/1/27? Can we structure credits if our usage ramps slowly over Q1? And how do overages work during ramp?

Also, compliance wants to see any SLA offsets tied to uptime and latency for dedicted capacity. Can you share a draft commercial that includes a ramp protection schedule?

—Arjun
Head of Infrastructure, NimbleHealth

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question and next steps

Arjun —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a short proposal (RI_annual_commit_proposal_v1.pdf) that lays out two paths:

1) Flat 12‑month prepaid reserve (billed annually) — 18% unit discount vs monthly, true‑up at year end. Includes burst capacity at a pre‑agreed rate.
2) Staged tranche commit — 9mo/3mo split where 60% of the annual $ commit is billed upfront and the remaining 40% is invoiced after Q1 based on usage milestones; this path includes refundable credits to protect you if actual usage < milestone thresholds.

For ramp protection we propose a "safety tranche": if actual token usage in Q1 is <60% of forecast, NimbleHealth receives a one‑time credit equal to the difference in unit spend (up to 20% of the annual commit). Overages during ramp would bill at the committed unit rate until the tranche is exhausted, then at the overage rate (1.45x committed unit price).

SLA offsets are possible — we include a 10% credit cap tied to systemic outage windows beyond the SLA. I flagged finance and legal to expect a short redline.

If the staged tranche looks preferable I can draft language and a tranche schedule; otherwise I can share a simple one‑line service schedule for the flat prepay. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attach: RI_annual_commit_proposal_v1.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question and next steps

Looping in pricing ops and finance. Notes for negotiation:
- Avoid refundable cash — prefer crediting to future invoices to keep accounting clean.
- For the tranche proposal, limit refundable credit to a one‑time invoice offset and cap it (20% is okay but legal will push).
- Suggest adding a quarterly true‑up with 30‑day notice windows rather than a single year‑end true‑up. Helps both sides spot divergence early.
- Confirm that reserved capacity can be reallocated across regions if NimbleHealth replicates services (region clause).

I'll prepare a sample tranche schedule (commit_ramp_schedule.xlsx) and one redline for the legal team to review.

-Marissa

From: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@nimblehealth.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: procurements@nimblehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-02T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question and next steps

Thanks Logan/Marissa —

The staged tranche path sounds promising, particularly if credits are ledgered against future invoices (finance prefers that). A few clarifying points before we proceed to legal:
1) Can we cap annual price increases for committed years (we're evaluating a 2‑year option)?
2) For the SLA credit, can you convert "10% credit cap" to a clear formula and example so compliance can sign off quickly?
3) DocuSign flow: procurement needs individual invoices aligned to tranche billings (we cannot accept a single lump invoice that doesn't itemize the tranches).

If you can send the tranche schedule and a draft with invoice line examples, we'll fast‑track to legal. Also, if you can provide a short example that shows the worst‑case and best‑case cashflows for NimbleHealth for the first 6 months, that will expedite CFO approval.

—Arjun

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question and next steps

Arjun —

Attaching the tranche schedule and a cleaned commercial summary. Key updates based on your asks and our internal notes:
- 2‑year cap: we can fix committed unit price for 12 months; for a 24‑month contract we'll offer a 6% floor protection on price increases year two (i.e., any list increase above 6% is absorbed by Redwood for committed units).
- SLA credit formula: (Total monthly committed spend) x (downtime minutes beyond SLA / total minutes in month) x 0.5 = credit amount, capped at 10% of monthly committed spend. Example included in the PDF.
- Billing: we'll issue tranche invoices as separate line items in DocuSign and in our ERP so finance receives explicit tranche invoices.

I've uploaded the redline (Nimble_redline_v1.docx) with suggested language that uses invoice credits (not cash refunds). If that aligns I will send the DocuSign for signatures and route procurement invoices per tranche.

Next steps: let me know if procurement wants any different wording on invoice itemization; otherwise I'll queue the DocuSign by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attach: commit_ramp_schedule.xlsx, Nimble_redline_v1.docx, RI_annual_commit_proposal_v1.pdf
